title: Know When to Zoom: How Small Is Too Small for Vision-Language Models?
abstract: arXiv:2611.22709v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Online vision-language models often miss small details in large images, because the service shrinks the image, or rejects it, before the model ever sees it. A car 20 pixels wide in an 8000 by 6000 drone photo reaches Claude about 6 pixels wide, and OpenAI's default rejects the photo outright. We measure how much detail survives for seven models from four vendors, using an eye exam of printed codes and 601 questions about small objects in real photos. The smallest text a model reads half the time grows from 6 pixels or less on a small image to a predicted 10 to 13 pixels on a 7680 by 4320 photo at default settings. Zooming wins much of the detail back. Splitting each photo into up to nine tiles raises accuracy by 11.1 to 14.5 percentage points for Claude and Gemini, and by avoiding rejections it lifts GPT-6.1 Sol from 50.7% to 83.7%. translated_title: 知道何时缩放：对视觉语言模型而言，多小才算太小？
translated_abstract: 在线视觉语言模型常常遗漏大图像中的微小细节，因为服务在模型看到图像之前就将其缩小，甚至直接拒收。在一张8000×6000的无人机照片中宽20像素的汽车，到达Claude时大约只剩6像素宽，而OpenAI的默认设置则会直接拒绝这张照片。我们通过印刷代码的“视力测试”以及601个关于真实照片中小物体的问题，测量了四家厂商七款模型有多少细节得以保留。在默认设置下，模型能以50%概率正确读取的最小文本尺寸，在小图像上为6像素或更小，而在7680×4320照片上预计增长到10至13像素。缩放（放大）能挽回大部分丢失的细节：将每张照片切分为最多九个图块，可使Claude和Gemini的准确率提高11.1至14.5个百分点，并通过避免拒收使GPT-6.1 Sol的准确率从50.7%提升至83.7%。一种两步缩放方法——即模型先指出它所需的区域——在Gemini上的表现与图块切分方法相当甚至更优……
tldr: 该研究量化了主流在线视觉语言模型因服务端缩图或拒收而在大图像上损失的细节，并证明简单的图块切分和“先定位再缩放”的两步策略能大幅恢复模型对小物体和微小文字的识别准确率。
en_tdlr: This study quantifies how much fine detail online vision-language models lose when large images are downscaled or rejected by services, and shows that simple tiling and a two-step "locate-then-zoom" strategy substantially recover accuracy on small objects and tiny text.
